'''Dean Jackson Wade''' (born November 20, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State Wildcats]].

==Early life==
Wade was born in [[Wichita, Kansas]], to Jay and Trish Wade. He lived in [[Inman, Kansas]], briefly before moving to [[St. John, Kansas|St. John]] at a young age.<ref name="bio">{{cite web|title=Dean Wade|url=https://www.kstatesports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/dean-wade/5623|publisher=Kansas State Sports|access-date=July 28, 2026}}</ref> His mother is a [[track and field|track]] and [[volleyball]] coach at [[St. John High School]] in [[St. John, Kansas]], where she led the volleyball team to three state championships.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 22, 2018 |title=Dean Wade highlights home town's rich athletic tradition |url=https://www.kwch.com/content/news/Dean-Wade-highlights-home-towns-rich-basketball-tradition-477688733.html |access-date=March 24, 2018 |publisher=[[KWCH-DT]]}}</ref> His father was briefly a member of the [[Kansas State Wildcats|football team]] at [[Kansas State University]].<ref name="hero">{{cite web|last=Robinett|first=Kellis|title=As Dean Wade leads K-State into NCAA Tournament, he's become a Kansas small-town hero|url=http://www.kansas.com/sports/college/big-12/kansas-state/article204934374.html|website=[[The Wichita Eagle]]|access-date=March 24, 2018|date=March 16, 2018}}</ref>

==High school career==
Wade played four years of [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball at St. John High School in [[St. John, Kansas]], earning All-State honors for multiple seasons and winning three state championships.<ref name=bio/> As a senior, he was named [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]], along with 29 other players in his class.<ref name="parade">{{cite web|last=Robinett|first=Kellis|title=Incoming Kansas State freshman Dean Wade named Parade All-American|url=http://www.kansas.com/sports/varsity-kansas/article162450788.html|website=[[The Wichita Eagle]]|access-date=March 24, 2018|date=June 1, 2015}}</ref> He was also selected as [[Mr. Kansas Basketball]] by the Kansas Basketball Coaches Association (KBCA).<ref name="mrbasketball">{{cite web |date=March 30, 2015 |title=Wade Named Mr. Kansas Basketball |url=https://www.kstatesports.com/news/2015/3/30/5583f3c8e4b06b726e6673fe_131478095500428120.aspx |access-date=June 5, 2023 |publisher=Kansas State Sports}}</ref>

==College career==
Wade was named to the [[Big 12]] All-Newcomer Team at the conclusion of his freshman season at [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]].<ref name=bio/> As a sophomore, he averaged 9.3 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game.<ref name="realgm">{{cite web|title=Dean Wade|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Dean-Wade/Summary/84884|publisher=[[RealGM]]|access-date=March 24, 2018}}</ref> After a breakout junior season, Wade earned first-team All-Big 12 accolades.<ref>{{cite web|last=Robinett|first=Kellis|title=Kansas State forward Dean Wade makes All-Big 12 first team, Barry Brown lands on second team|url=http://www.kansas.com/sports/college/big-12/kansas-state/article203432404.html|website=[[The Wichita Eagle]]|access-date=March 24, 2018|date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> Wade averaged 16.2 points and 6.2 rebounds per game as a junior.<ref>{{cite web|last=Robinett|first=Kellis|title=What are the odds K-State juniors Barry Brown, Dean Wade test NBA Draft waters|url=http://www.kansas.com/sports/college/big-12/kansas-state/article206781369.html|website=[[The Wichita Eagle]]|access-date=May 29, 2018|date=March 25, 2018}}</ref> As a senior, Wade averaged 12.9 points and a team-high 6.2 rebounds per game and was named to the first-team All-Big 12. His season was cut short by a foot injury.<ref>{{cite news|last=Black|first=Ryan|title=K-State senior forward Dean Wade 'doubtful' to play in NCAA Tournament|url=https://themercury.com/k_state_sports/k-state-senior-forward-dean-wade-doubtful-to-play-in/article_103c4310-1eba-545c-b24e-f8551072cbb0.html|access-date=June 21, 2019|work=The Manhattan Mercury|date=March 19, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Cleveland Cavaliers (2019–2026)===

==== 2019–20 season ====
[[File:Dean Wade shots, Cavaliers vs San Lorenzo on October 2019 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Wade attempts a shot in an October 2019 exhibition game.]]
On July 9, 2019, Wade signed a two-way contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] after going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Gold |first=Matthew |date=July 9, 2019 |title=Cavs Sign Dean Wade to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/dean-wade-signing-190709 |access-date=July 9, 2019 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On November 18, Wade made his NBA debut against the [[New York Knicks]], he went scoreless but logged one steal in eight minutes of action.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dean Wade 2019-20 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/wadede01/gamelog/2020/|access-date=2021-04-03|website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> Wade only played 12 games with the Cavaliers during his rookie season, averaging 1.7 points and 1.6 rebounds in six minutes of play.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=2020-06-29 |title=Cavaliers sign rookie Dean Wade to a multi-year NBA contract |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2020/06/29/cavaliers-sign-rookie-dean-wade-to-a-multi-year-nba-contract/ |access-date=2021-04-03 |website=The Rookie Wire}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Russo|first=Kelsey|title=Dean Wade finds confidence in game, makes leap to Cavs after season in G League|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1928487/2020/07/22/dean-wade-finds-confidence-in-game-makes-leap-to-cavs-after-season-in-g-league/|access-date=2021-04-03|website=The Athletic}}</ref><ref name=":2"/> He spent most of the season with the Cavaliers' [[G League]] affiliate, the [[Canton Charge]]. In the G League, Wade started in 29 of 30 games, averaging 14.2 points, 7.6 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.4 blocks in 31.1 minutes while shooting 46.1% from the field and 39.9% from three-point range.<ref name=":0"/><ref name=":1"/><ref name=":2"/>

==== 2020–21 season ====
[[File:Dean Wade (51177401735).jpg|thumb|upright|left|Wade during warm-ups in a May 2021 game]]
On July 2, 2020, Wade signed a multi-year deal with the Cavaliers.<ref name=":2">{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Nick |date=June 30, 2020 |title=Cavaliers Sign Dean Wade and Jordan Bell To Multi-Year Contracts |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/bell-wade-signing-200630 |access-date=June 30, 2020 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

[[File:Dean Wade vs Norman Powell, Cleveland Cavaliers vs Portland Trail Blazers on November 3, 2021 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Wade driving towards the basket as [[Norman Powell]] guards him in November 2021]]

==== 2022–23 season ====
On June 22, 2022, the Cavaliers announced they exercised their fourth-year team option on Wade, keeping him with the team for another season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 22, 2022 |title=Cavaliers Exercise Fourth-Year Team Option on Dean Wade |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/cavaliers-exercise-fourth-year-team-option-on-dean-wade |access-date=2022-06-24 |website=NBA.com }}</ref> On September 26, Wade signed a three-year, $18.5 million contract extension with the team.<ref>{{Cite tweet|user=cavs|number=1574768486404001792|title=.OFFICIAL: #Cavs sign Dean Wade to multi-year contract extension|author=Cleveland Cavaliers|access-date=October 1, 2022}}</ref> On October 30, 2022, Wade scored a career high of 22 points shooting 6 of 8 from three versus the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 31, 2022 |title=New York Knicks at Cleveland Cavaliers Box Score, October 30, 2022 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202210300CLE.html |access-date=April 6, 2023 |website=Basketball Reference}}</ref> That night, Wade, [[Kevin Love]] and [[Donovan Mitchell]] set the NBA record for most three-pointers made by three different teammates in a single game, scoring a total of 22 threes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 31, 2022 |title=22 THREES BY THREE — the most by a trio of teammates in a game in NBA history. 👌 #LetEmKnow |url=https://x.com/cavs/status/1587127367176175620 |access-date=April 6, 2023 |website=Twitter}}</ref>

==== 2023–24 season ====
On March 5, 2024, Wade scored a career-high 23 points, with 20 of them coming in the fourth quarter, spearheading a 22-point comeback win over the [[Boston Celtics]]—the largest fourth-quarter comeback in Cavaliers franchise history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lloyd |first=Jason |title=Lloyd: This is the Dean Wade the Cavs expected. Now they have to solve a 'big' riddle |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5321002/2024/03/06/cleveland-cavs-dean-wade-celtics/ |access-date=2024-03-06 |website=The Athletic |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2024–25 season ====
During the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024-25 NBA season]], Wade appeared in 59 games (30 starts) for the Cavaliers, averaging 5.4 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.3 assists.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Dean Wade {{!}} Forward-Center {{!}} Cleveland Cavaliers |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1629731/dean-wade |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2025–26 season ====
During the [[2025–26 NBA season]], Wade appeared in 59 games (38 starts) for the Cavaliers, averaging 5.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.5 assists.<ref name=":3"/>

=== Philadelphia 76ers (2026–present) ===
On July 6, 2026, Wade signed a four–year, $39 million contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=PHILADELPHIA 76ERS SIGN DEAN WADE |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76erssign-dean-wade |access-date=2026-07-28 |website=NBA.com |language=en|date=2026-07-06|last=Murphy|first=Matt}}</ref>
